title: Fresenius Medical Care reports third quarter 2026 performance partially offsetting headwinds and narrowing full year outlook
body_markdown:
### Strategic progress


Fresenius Medical Care, the world’s leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal disease, continues to focus on execution to improve core operations and to drive profitable growth.


The large-scale U.S. commercial rollout of the innovative **5008X CAREsystem** is progressing as planned. Since its launch in early 2026, approximately 16% of dialysis machines in Fresenius Medical Care’s U.S. clinics have been replaced, keeping the company on track to reach its full-year target of around 20%. As adoption expands, treatments performed with the system have risen to 1.3 million, including more than 500,000 HDF treatments and more than 300,000 HvHDF treatments. Early observations are directionally better than previously published real-world data associating HvHDF with fewer hospitalizations, fewer missed treatments, and improved survival compared with conventional hemodialysis. At ASN Kidney Week in Denver, Colorado, we presented updates demonstrating the ability to achieve HvHDF for U.S. patients, with typical treatment times, blood and dialysate flows during therapy and look forward to presenting data in publications and congresses specifically around patient experience, hospitalizations, and survival through 2027.


In October, Fresenius Medical Care launched the **multiFiltratePRO™** system in the U.S. for critically ill patients with acute kidney injury (AKI). The system continuously cleans the blood, removing waste and extra fluid when a patient’s kidneys can no longer do this on their own. multiFiltratePRO is the first FDA-cleared continuous kidney replacement therapy (CKRT) system in the U.S. for regional citrate anticoagulation using the Ci-Ca Protocol. The system brings important treatment steps together in one place, helping make a complex therapy easier for healthcare professionals to manage so they can focus on patient care.


The launch followed FDA clearance of multiFiltratePRO and approval of Cienby™, a sodium citrate solution, and Calrezdy™, a calcium chloride solution. Together, these advances reflect Fresenius Medical Care’s longstanding experience in developing and bringing complex kidney therapies to patients around the world.


In **China** , the company refined its commercial strategy by discontinuing production and sales of the 4008A hemodialysis system locally and exited its peritoneal dialysis (PD) business while maintaining existing obligations in the market. The resulting one-time costs of EUR 108 million are primarily attributable to impairment charges, scrappage and termination costs, treated as a special item in Care Enablement.


During the third quarter of 2026, the **FME25+ transformation program** delivered EUR 74 million additional sustainable savings while related one-time costs, treated as special items amounted to EUR 54 million. The company expects EUR 250 million savings and EUR 350 million related one-time costs in 2026. FME25+ savings are expected to total EUR 1.2 billion by the end of 2027.


As part of the capital allocation framework, **share buyback programs** complement shareholder returns through dividends. On May 26, a second program for a total volume of around EUR 1 billion (excluding ancillary costs) was announced and is being executed in tranches within 12 months. The first tranche was initiated on May 28 and is planned to end by December 15, 2026. As of September 30, 9.1 million shares or 3.4% of total shares issued have been repurchased for a total investment of EUR 357 million.


### Organic revenue growth in Care Delivery and Care Enablement


In the **third quarter of 2026, Group** revenue increased by 1% compared to prior year (-1% at constant currency, +0.1% organic1) to EUR 4,937 million. Divestitures realized as part of the portfolio optimization plan negatively affected the revenue development by 30 basis points.


**Care Delivery** revenue increased by 3% (+1% at constant currency, +2% organic1) to EUR 3,492 million. Divestitures realized as part of the portfolio optimization plan negatively affected the revenue development by 40 basis points.


In Care Delivery U.S., revenue increased by 3% (+1% at constant currency, +1% organic1) to EUR 2,920 million. Favorable rate effects were offset by the TDAPA reimbursement regulations headwind as expected. U.S. same market treatment growth came in at -1.1%.


In Care Delivery International, revenue increased by 2% (+3% at constant currency, +6% organic1) to EUR 572 million, driven by positive organic growth1. International same market treatment growth amounted to 1.4%.


**Value-Based Care** revenue declined by 7% (-9% at constant currency, -9% organic1) to EUR 537 million. The development in the quarter was driven by the changed risk contracting for one of the contracts, partially offset by positive effects from payor premium rates and prior-year phasing of CKCC reporting from CMS.


**Care Enablement** revenue increased by 7% (+5% at constant currency, +5% organic1) to EUR 1,451 million. Positive pricing globally and positive volume development outside China were mainly driven by the sales of 5008X CAREsystem.


Within **Inter-segment eliminations** 5, revenue for services provided and products transferred between the operating segments at fair market value came in at negative EUR 543 million.


In the **first nine months of 2026, Group** revenue decreased by 1% (+2% at constant currency, +3% organic¹) to EUR 14,409 million. Currency effects negatively impacted revenue development in all three operating segments. Divestitures realized as part of the portfolio optimization plan negatively impacted the revenue development by 40 basis points. **Care Delivery** revenue remained flat (+4% at constant currency, +5% organic1) at EUR 10,264 million, with Care Delivery U.S. flat (+4% at constant currency, +5 organic1) at EUR 8,582 million and Care Delivery International flat (+2% at constant currency, +7% organic1) at EUR 1,682 million. Divestitures realized as part of the portfolio optimization plan negatively affected the revenue development of Care Delivery by 70 basis points and the revenue development of Care Delivery International by 3,900 basis points. U.S. same market treatment growth came in at -0.8% while international same market treatment growth amounted to 1.2%. **Value-Based Care** revenue decreased by 3% (+1% at constant currency, +1% organic1) to EUR 1,563 million. **Care Enablement** revenue increased by 1% (+3% at constant currency, +3% organic1) to EUR 4,121 million. Inter-segment eliminations came in at negative EUR 1,539 million.


### Earnings development in line with planned full-year phasing


In the **third quarter of 2026, Group** operating income declined by 19% (-19% at constant currency) to EUR 384 million, resulting in a margin of 7.8% (Q3 2025: 9.8%). Operating income excluding special items declined by 5% (-6% at constant currency) to EUR 545 million, resulting in a margin2 of 11.0% (Q3 2025: 11.7%).


Operating income in **Care Delivery** increased by 18% (+17% at constant currency) to EUR 497 million, resulting in a margin of 14.2% (Q3 2025: 12.3%). Operating income excluding special items increased by 4% (+2% at constant currency) to EUR 513 million, resulting in a margin2 of 14.7% (Q3 2025: 14.5%). Compared to previous year, the improvement was driven by positive rate effects, as well as savings from the FME25+ program, offsetting negative impacts from TDAPA reimbursement regulations and increased labor costs.


Operating income in **Value-Based Care** improved to a breakeven in the quarter from a loss of EUR 22 million in the prior year, resulting in a margin of 0.0% (Q3 2025: -3.8%) Operating income excluding special items improved to EUR 1 million compared to a loss of EUR 21 million in the prior year, resulting in a margin2 of 0.1% (Q3 2025: -3.7%) and reflecting the quarterly earnings volatility, which is inherent to the business model. The improvement was driven by the prior-year phasing of CKCC reporting by CMS, an enhanced savings rate and positive contributions from the FME25+ program.


Operating income in **Care Enablement** resulted in a loss of EUR 32 million and a margin of -2.2% (Q3 2025: 6.4%) mainly due to one-time costs related to the China strategy refinement. Operating income excluding special items increased by 3% (+4% at constant currency) to EUR 106 million, resulting in a margin2 of 7.3% (Q3 2025: 7.6%). Compared to the previous year’s quarter, increased sales of the 5008X CAREsystem, the FME25+ program as well as positive price globally and volume effects outside China contributed positively. This was offset mainly by accelerated inflationary cost increases.


Operating income for **Corporate** amounted to a loss of EUR 35 million (Q3 2025: loss of EUR 4 million). Operating income excluding special items amounted to a loss of EUR 29 million (Q3 2025: gain of EUR 3 million). The development was mainly driven by the planned costs for strategic IT platform investments, while the impact from virtual power purchase agreements was positive.


In the **first nine months of 2026, Group** operating income decreased by 8% (-5% at constant currency) to EUR 1,136 million, resulting in a margin of 7.9% (9M 2025: 8.5%). Operating income excluding special items increased by 5% (+8% at constant currency) to EUR 1,581 million, resulting in a margin2 of 11.0% (9M 2025: 10.3%). In **Care Delivery** , operating income increased by 11% (+16% at constant currency) to EUR 1,203 million, resulting in a margin of 11.7% (9M 2025: 10.6%). Operating income excluding special items increased by 17% (+23% at constant currency) to EUR 1,437 million, resulting in a margin2 of 14.0% (9M 2025: 12.0%). In **Value-Based Care** operating income improved to EUR 6 million compared to a loss of EUR 28 million in the prior year, resulting in a margin of 0.4% (9M 2025: -1.7%). Operating income excluding special items improved to EUR 27 million compared to a loss of EUR 26 million in the prior year, resulting in a margin2 of 1.7% (9M 2025: -1.6%). In **Care Enablement** , operating income declined by 43% (-42% at constant currency) to EUR 153 million, resulting in a margin of 3.7% (9M 2025: 6.6%). Operating income excluding special items declined by 2% (flat at constant currency) to EUR 329 million, resulting in a margin2 of 8.0% (9M 2025: 8.2%). Operating income for **Corporate** amounted to a loss of EUR 119 million (9M 2025: loss of EUR 78 million). Operating income excluding special items amounted to a loss of EUR 105 million (9M 2025: loss of EUR 9 million).


**Net income** 3 decreased by 42% compared to prior year (-41% at constant currency) to EUR 160 million in the **third quarter of 2026** . Net income excluding special items decreased by 10% (-10% at constant currency) to EUR 291 million.


In the **first nine months** of 2026, net income3 decreased by 24% (-21% at constant currency) to EUR 496 million. Net income excluding special items increased by 1% (+4% at constant currency) to EUR 844 million.


**Basic earnings per share (EPS)** decreased by 35% compared to prior year (-34% at constant currency) to EUR 0.61 in the **third quarter of 2026** , based on 262,951,005 shares. Basic EPS excluding special items remained flat (flat at constant currency) at EUR 1.11.


In the **first nine months of 2026** , basic EPS decreased by 17% (-14% at constant currency) to EUR 1.84, based on 268,833,509 shares. Basic EPS excluding special items increased by 10% (+13% at constant currency) to EUR 3.14.


### Strong operating cash flow, net leverage ratio stable around lower end of target corridor


In the **third quarter of 2026, operating cash flow** increased by 8% to EUR 798 million (Q3 2025: EUR 742 million), resulting in a margin of 16.2% (Q3 2025: 15.2%). In the **first nine months of 2026** , operating cash flow improved by 12% to EUR 1,885 million (9M 2025: EUR 1,679 million). The related margin came in at 13.1% (9M 2025: 11.5%). Both developments were mainly driven by favorable working capital development.


**Free cash flow** 6 increased by 3% to EUR 564 million in the **third quarter of 2026** (Q3 2025: EUR 550 million), resulting in a margin of 11.4% (Q3 2025: 11.3%). In the **first nine months of 2026** , Fresenius Medical Care increased free cash flow by 3% to EUR 1,229 million (9M 2025: EUR 1,199 million), resulting in a margin of 8.5% (9M 2025: 8.2%).


**Total net debt and lease liabilities** increased by 6% to EUR 9,787 million (Q3 2025: EUR 9,218 million). The net leverage ratio (net debt/EBITDA) remained stable at 2.6x in Q3 2026 (Q2 2026: 2.6x) and continues to be around the lower end of our 2.5x to 3.0x target band.


### Patients, clinics and employees


As of September 30, 2026, Fresenius Medical Care treated 289,014 **patients** in 3,512 **dialysis clinics** worldwide and had 106,291 **employees** globally.


### Outlook 2026 narrowed


Fresenius Medical Care continues to expect **revenue growth** 1 to be broadly flat in 2026 compared to prior year. The company narrows its outlook for operating income2 and now expects **operating income** 2 growth to be between flat and a negative mid-single digit percent growth rate compared to prior year.


The expected growth rates for 2026 are at constant currency and excluding special items in operating income. The 2025 basis for the revenue outlook is EUR 19,628 million and for the operating income outlook is EUR 2,212 million.


### Investor conference call


Fresenius Medical Care will host a conference call for analysts and investors to discuss the results of the third quarter, on November 3, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. CET / 8:00 a.m. ET. Details are available[here](https://freseniusmedicalcare.com/en/investors/publications/publications/) . A replay and a transcript will be available shortly after the call.


Please refer to our statement of earnings included at the end of this press release and to the attachments as separate PDF files for a complete overview of the results of the third quarter of 2026. Our form 6-K disclosure provides more details.


1 At constant currency, adjusted for certain reconciling items including revenue from acquisitions, closed or sold operations and differences in dialysis days


2 Adjusted for special items; growth rate at constant currency (if not stated otherwise); for further details please see the reconciliation attached to the press release


3 Net income attributable to shareholders of Fresenius Medical Care AG


4 Data as of Sep 30, 2026


5 The company transfers products from the Care Enablement segment to the Care Delivery segment at fair market value. Services provided by the Care Delivery segment for patients managed under the Value-Based Care segment are also provided at fair market value. The associated internal revenues and expenses and all other consolidation of transactions are included within “Inter-segment eliminations”.


6 Net cash provided by / used in operating activities, after capital expenditures, before acquisitions, investments, and dividends


About Fresenius Medical Care:
Fresenius Medical Care is the world's leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal diseases of which around 4.5 million patients worldwide regularly undergo dialysis treatment. Through its network of 3,512 dialysis clinics, Fresenius Medical Care provides dialysis treatments for approx. 290,000 patients around the globe. Fresenius Medical Care is also the leading provider of dialysis products such as dialysis machines or dialyzers. Fresenius Medical Care is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (FME) and on the New York Stock Exchange (FMS).
